groups.label: Look Back
items: Five years after the Revolution: The French Revolution begins in 1789 with the Storming of the Bastille. The slogan Liberté, égalité, fraternité was proclaimed — and five years later, in 1794, the National Convention extended it to enslaved populations in French territories.

Haitian Revolution trigger: The major slave revolt in Saint-Domingue began in 1791. It took 3 years of intense fighting on the island before Paris formally ratified full emancipation in 1794. The sequence: 1789 → 1791 → 1794.

groups.label: Year of 1794
items: 1794 is the height of the Reign of Terror — Robespierre is executed that same July. The National Convention was in its most radical phase, the same political energy that pushed through abolition.

Toussaint Louverture, the future leader of Haiti, was already a rising military commander in Saint-Domingue by 1794 — the same year France's decree legally caught up to the revolution already underway on the ground.

groups.label: Look Ahead
items: Napoleon reverses the decree in 1802 — just eight years later. A short-lived window of legal freedom under French law: 1794 to 1802.
Haiti declares full independence in 1804, ten years after France's abolition decree — a straight line from legal emancipation to the colony's break from France.

France was the first major European colonial power to abolish slavery in 1794. Britain followed: subtract 13 years to reach the abolition of the British slave trade in 1807, or 40 years to reach Britain's full abolition of slavery in 1834.

groups.label: Look Back
items: Count forward from Hertz: Heinrich Hertz proved electromagnetic waves exist in 1887–88. Marconi turns that pure theory into a practical device about 7-8 years later, in 1895.
Sequential Tech Link: Hertz (1887) → Marconi (1895). Eight years from 'waves exist' to 'send a message with them.'

groups.label: Year of 1895
items: 1895 was the birth year of two mass-communication technologies: wireless radio (Marconi) and cinema (Lumière brothers). Both born the same year.
The '1-8-9-5' bridge trick: Röntgen also discovered X-rays in 1895. Pair 'invisible waves' (X-rays) with 'invisible signals' (radio) — both in 1895.

groups.label: Look Ahead
items: Turn of the Century Anchor: 1895 = exactly 5 years before 1900. A late-Victorian invention, not a 1930s one.
Marconi → Atlantic → 1901: 1895 = local demo. Six years later, 1901 = transatlantic signal.
Titanic anchor: Wireless saved survivors in 1912. Subtract ~17 years → 1895, when the technology was first demonstrated.

groups.label: Look Back
items: Northern Kingdom anchor: The Kingdom of Israel (the North) fell to the Assyrians in 722 BCE. Judah (the South) survived for another 134 years before Jerusalem fell to Nebuchadnezzar II in 588–586 BCE.
Nebuchadnezzar II becomes king of Babylon in 605 BCE, the same year he crushes Egypt at Carchemish. Jerusalem's conquest follows about 17 years into his reign, in 588 BCE.

Count forward from the first deportation: Babylon exiles King Jehoiachin and part of Jerusalem's elite in 597 BCE. The final conquest and the Temple's destruction come about nine years later, in 588 BCE.

groups.label: Year of 588 BCE
items: 588 BCE comes just one generation after Babylon itself broke free of Assyrian rule in 626 BCE — the new Babylonian Empire wasted little time turning to conquer its neighbors.
Greek philosopher Thales of Miletus predicts a solar eclipse around 585 BCE, just three years after Jerusalem's fall — a useful cross-check if you know early Greek science dates.

groups.label: Look Ahead
items: Cyrus the Great conquers Babylon in 539 BCE, ending the exile. Subtract 49 years from that to land on 588 BCE, when the exile began.
Second Temple bookend: Solomon's First Temple was destroyed by Babylon in 588/586 BCE. The Second Temple was destroyed by the Romans in 70 CE — over 650 years later.
